newsitem.title: USA: Carolina First to divest five S.C. units.
newsitem.headline: Carolina First to divest five S.C. units.

text.p: Carolina First Corp said on Monday it was divesting five branches in South Carolina to the newly-organized Bank of Barnwell County for an undisclosed sum.

The five banking offices had total deposits of about $50 million, the company said in a statement. The transaction, which was subject to regulatory approval, was due to be completed in January 1997, it said.

The branches were located in Barnwell, Blackville, Salley, Springfield and Williston, the company said. The Bank of Barnwell County was expected to be a wholly-owned subsidiary of Community Capital Corp of Greenwood, S.C., it said.

"Our decision to sell the five offices in no way reflects a shif in our strategy of being South Carolina's bank but merely permits Carolina First to focus our efforts," President and Chief Executive Officer Mack Whittle Jr. said in a statement.
Carolina First has 55 banking offices throughout South Carolina.
